title: Setting Up the Development Environment
description: Step-by-step guide to installing the .NET SDK, choosing a code editor, and verifying your setup is ready for ASP.NET Core development. Covers Windows, macOS, and Linux.

blocks.text: Before you can build ASP.NET Core applications, you need two main tools: the **.NET SDK** (Software Development Kit) and a **code editor**. The SDK includes everything needed to compile, run, and publish .NET apps, while the editor is where you will write and debug your code.
The good news is that both are free, cross-platform, and well-documented. This lesson walks you through installing them on Windows, macOS, or Linux.

The .NET SDK is the foundation for everything you will build. It includes the C# compiler, the `dotnet` command-line tool, libraries, and templates for creating new projects. We recommend using the latest **Long Term Support (LTS)** version, currently .NET 8 LTS, for production stability.

blocks.title: Use an LTS version
blocks.text: An LTS (Long Term Support) release receives security updates and bug fixes for three years. For learning and production, always choose the LTS version unless you need a specific newer feature.

blocks.title: Installation steps by platform
items: **Windows** — Download and run the installer from dotnet.microsoft.com, or use the `winget` command: `winget install Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.8`
**macOS** — Use Homebrew: `brew install --cask dotnet-sdk`. Alternatively, download the PKG installer from Microsoft.
**Linux** — Follow the distro-specific instructions at dotnet.microsoft.com, or use the package manager for your distribution (e.g., `apt` on Ubuntu).
**All platforms** — After installing, run `dotnet --version` in a terminal to confirm the version number appears.

blocks.text: You can write ASP.NET Core code in any text editor, but two editors provide the best experience with features like IntelliSense (code completion), debugging, and integrated terminal support.

blocks.title: Popular code editors for ASP.NET Core

cards.title: Visual Studio 2022
cards.description: Full-featured IDE for Windows and macOS. The most powerful option with designers, profilers, and excellent debugging.
pros: Rich designer tools for views and databases

cards.title: Visual Studio Code
cards.description: Lightweight, cross-platform code editor. Free and highly extensible with a thriving marketplace of extensions.
pros: Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux
Free with the C# Dev Kit extension
cons: Fewer built-in designers than Visual Studio
Requires extension setup for full experience

blocks.title: Verifying the .NET installation
blocks.content: Check the installed .NET SDK version and list available project templates.

blocks.text: The first command should display a version number like `8.0.100`. The second lists all installed SDK versions. The third shows all available project templates, including `mvc`, `webapi`, and `blazorserver`.

blocks.title: VS Code setup tip
blocks.text: If you use VS Code, install the **C# Dev Kit** extension from Microsoft. It adds IntelliSense, debugging, project management, and test integration. Restart VS Code after installing the extension.

terms.definition: The Software Development Kit that includes the C# compiler, dotnet CLI, project templates, and runtime needed to build and run .NET applications.
Long Term Support release — receives security updates and bug fixes for three years. .NET 8 LTS is the recommended version for learning and production.
The package manager for .NET. Dependencies are restored automatically when you build or run a project for the first time.
A Visual Studio Code extension that adds IntelliSense, debugging, and project management for C# and ASP.NET Core development.

blocks.text: When you install the .NET SDK, the runtime is included automatically. The runtime is what actually executes your compiled application on end-user machines. For development, the SDK is all you need. You only need to worry about separate runtime installations when deploying to servers.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting common problems
items: **'dotnet' command not found** — Restart your terminal after installing the SDK. On macOS/Linux, ensure the dotnet path is in your `PATH` environment variable.
**Wrong SDK version** — Run `dotnet --list-sdks` to see what is installed. Use `global.json` in your project folder to pin a specific SDK version.
**VS Code not recognizing C# files** — Ensure the C# Dev Kit extension is installed and enabled. Check the Output panel for any error messages.
**Port already in use** — On first run, ASP.NET Core uses ports 5000 and 5001. If another app is using them, add a `launchSettings.json` profile with different ports.

blocks.title: Set Up and Verify Your Environment
blocks.description: Complete your development environment setup and verify every component is working correctly.
steps: Download and install the .NET 8 SDK from dotnet.microsoft.com for your operating system
Install Visual Studio 2022 Community Edition (Windows) or VS Code with the C# Dev Kit (all platforms)
Open a new terminal and run `dotnet --version` to confirm the SDK is recognized
Run `dotnet new --list | findstr mvc` (Windows) or `dotnet new --list | grep mvc` (macOS/Linux) to find the MVC template
Open your editor and create a new empty folder to use as your workspace for this course
Run `dotnet new mvc -n TestApp` in that folder, then `cd TestApp` and `dotnet build` — confirm the build succeeds with no errors
blocks.expectedOutcome: The `dotnet build` command completes without errors, producing a `bin/` folder with compiled assemblies. This confirms your SDK, editor, and build tools are all correctly configured.

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: The .NET SDK is the essential toolkit — it includes the compiler, CLI, and project templates
Choose Visual Studio 2022 for a full IDE experience, or VS Code for a lightweight cross-platform editor
Always verify your setup by running `dotnet --version` and `dotnet new --list`
LTS versions of the .NET SDK are recommended for stability and long-term support
The C# Dev Kit extension for VS Code provides the closest experience to Visual Studio
blocks.takeaway: A properly set up development environment is the foundation of productive ASP.NET Core development. Once the SDK and editor are installed and verified, you are ready to start building.
